name: superhuman
title: Superhuman
description: Drive your inbox with Raycast AI. Draft, send, summarize, search, and triage email; check availability and create calendar events — all by mentioning @superhuman. Built on Superhuman's official MCP server.
author: jlokos

commands.name: placeholder
commands.title: Placeholder
commands.description: Placeholder until extensions no longer require a command

commands.name: skill-morning-briefing
commands.title: Morning Briefing
commands.description: Overnight inbox triage plus today's calendar summary. Opens the skill prompt and copies it for Quick AI.

commands.name: skill-eod-wrapup
commands.title: End-Of-Day Wrap-Up
commands.description: End-of-day summary: emails sent, replies received, meetings held, plus a preview of tomorrow's calendar.

commands.name: skill-meeting-scheduler
commands.title: Meeting Scheduler
commands.description: Resolve participants, find a free slot for everyone, and create the calendar invite with a video link.

commands.name: skill-deal-tracker
commands.title: Deal Tracker
commands.description: Track deals across email and calendar by querying recent threads, replies, and meetings for a named deal or company.

commands.name: skill-batch-draft-writer
commands.title: Batch Draft Writer
commands.description: Generate drafts across many threads from a single set of instructions. Useful for templated follow-ups and backlog triage.

tools.name: draft-email
tools.title: Draft Email
tools.description: Create or update a Superhuman draft via the MCP create_or_update_draft tool. Supports recipient, cc, bcc, subject, and body. Always pass full email addresses.

tools.name: query-email-and-calendar
tools.title: Search Email & Calendar
tools.description: Flagship cross-source search and Q&A across email + calendar + contacts. Supports natural language and Superhuman operators (from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment, is:unread, before:, after:, etc.).

tools.name: search-inbox
tools.title: Search Email & Calendar (Legacy Alias)
tools.description: Deprecated: use query-email-and-calendar. Kept so existing workflows continue to work; delegates to the new tool.

tools.name: send-draft
tools.title: Send Draft
tools.description: Send an existing Superhuman draft by id. Requires a confirmation before sending.

tools.name: discard-draft
tools.title: Discard Draft
tools.description: Permanently discard a Superhuman draft. Requires confirmation.

tools.name: undo-send
tools.title: Undo Send
tools.description: Recall the most recently sent email if Superhuman's undo-send window has not elapsed.

tools.name: get-thread
tools.title: Get Thread
tools.description: Fetch a full email thread (subject, participants, all messages) so the AI can summarize or read it.

tools.name: get-message
tools.title: Get Message
tools.description: Fetch a single email message by id (headers, body, attachment metadata).

tools.name: list-threads
tools.title: List Threads
tools.description: List recent email threads, optionally filtered by label or split. Use search-inbox for free-text queries.

tools.name: list-labels
tools.title: List Labels
tools.description: List all labels in the user's Superhuman account.

tools.name: list-splits
tools.title: List Splits
tools.description: List Superhuman inbox splits (e.g. Important, Other, News, Calendar) and their ids.

tools.name: get-attachment
tools.title: Get Attachment
tools.description: Retrieve a message attachment by message and attachment id (returns metadata and/or content as provided by Superhuman).

tools.name: get-read-status-feed
tools.title: Read Status Feed
tools.description: Get the Superhuman read-status feed: which recipients have opened recent tracked emails and when.

tools.name: mark-spam
tools.title: Mark as Spam
tools.description: Mark a thread as spam. Requires confirmation.

tools.name: trash-thread
tools.title: Trash Thread
tools.description: Move a thread to trash. Requires confirmation.

tools.name: unsubscribe
tools.title: Unsubscribe
tools.description: Unsubscribe from the mailing list that sent a given thread. Requires confirmation.

tools.name: update-thread
tools.title: Update Thread
tools.description: Update a thread: archive/unarchive, mark read/unread, star/unstar, add or remove labels.

tools.name: update-personalization
tools.title: Update Personalization
tools.description: Update Superhuman personalization by passing a single natural-language feedback string (e.g. 'I prefer Hey over Dear'). The server interprets the feedback and updates the relevant personalization model.

tools.name: create-or-update-event
tools.title: Create or Update Event
tools.description: Create a new calendar event or update an existing one. Requires confirmation when attendees are set.

tools.name: get-availability
tools.title: Get Availability
tools.description: Get free/busy availability for the user (and optionally other attendees) over a time range.

preferences.name: enableDraftPreviews
preferences.title: Draft Preferences
preferences.label: Enable Draft Previews
preferences.description: Show a preview of the email before creating it, allowing you to review before the draft is created in Superhuman.

preferences.name: readOnlyMode
preferences.title: Safety
preferences.label: Read-only mode
preferences.description: Block every write action (send, draft, archive, label, calendar create, personalization, etc.). All read tools (search, list, get) keep working. Useful when previewing how the AI would respond without risking unintended changes.

ai.instructions:
This extension drives Superhuman through Superhuman's official MCP server (https://mcp.mail.superhuman.com/mcp).

General rules:
- For email composition use draft-email, NOT query-email-and-calendar / search-inbox.
- Prefer the `instructions` field on draft-email (natural-language; Superhuman's AI writer composes in the user's voice). Only use `body` when you need a literal HTML body. Either is required; `type: forward` requires `body` (intro only — server appends the quoted message).
- For replies / forwards / reply-alls, set `type` AND pass the source `threadId` and `messageId`.
- Always pass full email addresses (e.g. "alex@example.com"), never just first names. If only a first name is given and no other context provides an address, append "@example.com".
- When the user gives multiple "To" recipients, pass them all in `recipient` as a comma-separated list — NOT in cc/bcc.
- Never produce Markdown links like [text](url). Provide complete URLs in plain text. Always include FULL meeting URLs (Zoom etc.) with all query parameters.
- For send-draft, discard-draft, trash-thread, mark-spam, unsubscribe, update-personalization, draft-email, and create-or-update-event with attendees: a confirmation dialog is shown — present the user with what will happen.
- send-draft scheduling options (`smartSend`, `sendAt`, `undoTimeout`) are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — pass at most one. When `undoTimeout` (1–10 min) is set, the response includes an `undoToken` you can pass to undo-send.
- After draft-email returns a draft id, chain send-draft if the user said to send.

Search and Q&A (query-email-and-calendar):
- query-email-and-calendar is the flagship cross-source tool — use it for natural-language questions across email + calendar + contacts.
- search-inbox still works; it delegates to query-email-and-calendar.
- Use lowercase operators with NO space after the colon: from:john, subject:budget, has:attachment.
- Do not wrap operator values in quotes.
- For "from John" queries, format as "from:john".
- For multi-word subjects, use "subject:multi word" without quotes.
- Do not add scopes like in:inbox unless the user explicitly asks.

Reading and triage:
- To answer questions about specific email, chain list-threads or query-email-and-calendar → get-thread (or get-message) so the AI can read actual content.
- list-threads now supports a full filter set: from[], to[], subjectContains, bodyContains, labels[], split (name or id), startDate, endDate, isUnread, isStarred, hasAttachment.
- For attachments, find the message via get-thread/get-message, then call get-attachment with the message id; pass `attachmentName` to pick a specific file.
- update-thread uses `markDone`, `markRead`, `markStarred`, `markImportant`, `addLabels`, `removeLabels`, `moveToFolder`. Old field names (`archived`, `read`, `starred`) still work but are deprecated.
- mark-spam can also `alsoBlockSender`, `alsoBlockDomain`, `alsoTrash` — surface these in the confirmation.

Calendar:
- create-or-update-event REQUIRES `timezone` (IANA, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"). Pass `conference: true` to add a video link. Use `recurrence` (RRULE) and `reminders` for repeating events.
- get-availability uses `participants` (names or emails — server resolves names), `timezone` (required), `startDate`/`endDate`, `durationMinutes`, `workingHoursOnly`.

Personalization:
- update-personalization takes a single freeform `feedback` string. Example: "I prefer 'Hey' over 'Dear'" or "My title is now VP Eng". The server interprets the feedback and updates the relevant personalization model.

Read-only mode:
- The user can enable a "Read-only mode" preference that blocks every write tool. If the user asks for an action that requires writing while this is on, surface the blocking dialog and stop — do not try to bypass it.

When combining with other Raycast AI extensions (Google Calendar, GitHub, Notion, Things), gather details first from the other extension, then call draft-email directly with the assembled information.

scripts.prepublishOnly:
echo "

It seems like you are trying to publish the Raycast extension to npm.

If you did intend to publish it to npm, remove the \`prepublishOnly\` script and rerun \`npm publish\` again.
If you wanted to publish it to the Raycast Store instead, use \`npm run publish\` instead.

" && exit 1
